In the context of adjective ordering, "whittling" functions as a **Material** (or a participle acting as a material descriptor, similar to "whittling wood" or "whittling tool"), not a **Purpose**. The standard order is Origin before Material. Therefore, "Nigerian" (Origin) must precede "whittling" (Material). My previous deduction that "whittling" was a Purpose led to a correct conclusion for the wrong reason, but the core error was the categorization. In future attempts, I will strictly classify adjectives: if an adjective is a participle describing what something is made of or its nature (like "whittling," "running," "sleeping"), I will treat it as Material or a specific descriptor that follows Origin. I will apply the sequence: Opinion > Size > Age > Shape > Color > Origin > Material > Purpose. Since Nigerian is Origin and whittling is Material, the order is Nigerian then whittling, confirming (B). I will ignore semantic oddities and rely solely on this strict categorical hierarchy.
